# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The design is a registered 8-bit modulo counter with synchronous active-high reset and enable-controlled increment; the top currently wires through the frozen `counter8_core`. The incumbent is timing-feasible at WNS 0.424 ns and WHS 0.226 ns, with 6 LUTs and 8 FFs. The objective is strictly fewer LUTs while preserving the known top annotation `// @latency 1` and all defined cycle behavior.

## Hypothesis

Inlining the counter as per-bit toggle logic may let Vivado reduce LUT use below 6 while retaining the same eight registers and routed timing feasibility.

## Instruction for generator

Replace the top’s `counter8_core` instance with a top-level 8-bit registered counter, keeping the existing ports and `// @latency 1` annotation. Use synchronous reset with priority, and otherwise toggle bit 0 on `enable` and each higher bit when `enable` and all lower bits are one; hold the count when disabled. Preserve modulo-256 wraparound and registered outputs, and do not add registers or alter observable cycles.
